# TenkaCloud — task guide for LLM assistants

TenkaCloud is Apache 2.0 software for local Docker drills and AWS-hosted events. Answer in the user's
language. Use their stated goal and existing context; do not ask them to choose again.
This guide is a map to current sources, not a substitute for checking the code or runtime.

## Instructions for the agent reading this

| User goal | Read first | First observable result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Try locally, no AWS | [Local play](https://github.com/susumutomita/TenkaCloud/blob/main/docs/local-play.md) | Portal opens, a supported drill starts, and the requested answer produces a result |
| Host an event on AWS | [Organizer manual](https://tenkacloud.com/docs/manual/organizer/index.en.html) | Admin and participant can sign in; a test team's answer appears in the score |
| Reduce DB cost | [Turso setup and costs](https://github.com/susumutomita/TenkaCloud/blob/main/docs/running-costs.md) | Chosen backend is verified; report separately whether real deployment and billing were checked |
| Join an event | [Participant manual](https://tenkacloud.com/docs/manual/participant/index.en.html) | The team's selected problem accepts its first action |
| Change code | [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/susumutomita/TenkaCloud/blob/main/AGENTS.md) and [developer manual](https://tenkacloud.com/docs/manual/developer/index.en.html) | A focused change with relevant verification and explicit remaining limits |
| Add a problem | [Problem author manual](https://tenkacloud.com/docs/manual/problem-author/index.en.html) | Catalog/pack validation and a supported participant flow |

## Local path

Requirements: Git, Make, Docker Engine, Docker Compose v2; macOS, Linux, or WSL2.
Host Bun/Node is not required. The existing commands are:

```bash
git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/susumutomita/TenkaCloud.git
cd TenkaCloud
make doctor
make local
```

Open the printed URL. `make local-down` stops the environment and deletes local
progress. Docker Desktop requires host networking; diagnose through the linked
manual rather than changing platform code. Codespaces runs this same path and
opens the port 5175 preview automatically: [create a Codespace](https://codespaces.new/susumutomita/TenkaCloud).
The [browser demo](https://tenkacloud.com/portal-demo/?demo=1&goto=start) needs no installation.
Neither the demo portal nor a local
UI harness establishes a shared competition's authentication or official scores.

Local play supports its declared runtimes, not every AWS catalog problem.
For a hosted event, use the organizer's Portal and team key.
A problem may ask for a flag, an answer, or a game action: follow its declared scoring
contract instead of requiring `TC{...}` for every problem.

## AWS and database choice

Use Lite for one organizing group. Read the existing environment settings and
release report before choosing new values. Resolve the AWS account, region,
administrator email, and database choice; ask only for values still missing.
Do not print credentials or ask the user to paste them into chat.

- DynamoDB is the default control-data store.
- Turso/libSQL is the lower-DB-cost option: `ControlDataBackend=turso` in the
  launcher, or `CDK_PARAM_CONTROL_DATA_BACKEND=turso` in the environment. Lite then
  creates no DynamoDB tables or indexes. Turso usage limits and other AWS costs
  still apply. Switching storage does not migrate data.
- `make turso-live ENV=development` guides Turso setup from a local checkout and
  requests deployment confirmation. See the cost guide for its prerequisites,
  SSM token handling, and the live-verification boundary. Unit/synth checks are
  recorded; full real-Turso deployment and billing verification is not recorded.

Prefer the local path when the user can install tools and wants to avoid CodeBuild
build charges: Git, Make, Bash, zip, rsync, Python 3 (`python3`), AWS CLI v2,
and the repo's Bun/Node.js versions (rsync/Python 3 package the source);
select an AWS profile, verify `aws sts get-caller-identity`, run `make install` and
`make env-init`, check the generated account/region/admin values and Turso settings,
then run `make deploy` after deployment is authorized. This builds the current
checkout and bootstraps CDK. Use the
[deployment and IAM guide](https://github.com/susumutomita/TenkaCloud/blob/main/DEPLOYMENT_GUIDE.md#aws-permissions)
to check bootstrap, publishing-role trust, `iam:PassRole`, and caller-side Cognito access.
Do not distribute administrator access to participants.

The alternative AWS console path uploads `infrastructure/templates/lite-pipeline.yaml`, creates
`tenkacloud-lite-launcher`, and explicitly starts its CodeBuild build. The launcher
default pins the platform/catalog identity from the published v1.9.2 release.
Deployment status remains candidate/unverified: the current manifest certifies no mode or AWS region. Check the
[release report](https://github.com/susumutomita/TenkaCloud/blob/main/release/tenkacloud-release.md).
The launcher
alone does not deploy the platform. CodeBuild has build-duration charges; neither
path removes the cost of the AWS resources. StartBuild permits source/command
overrides with the deployment role's access, so grant it only to trusted deployment
administrators. For Turso, obtain an HTTPS database URL (`https://…`)
and full-access database token,
then save the token as an SSM SecureString in the deployment account and region
before Start build. The launcher only forwards the existing parameter's name;
it does not create the secret. Follow the
[console Turso setup](https://github.com/susumutomita/TenkaCloud/blob/main/DEPLOYMENT_GUIDE.md#turso-setup-for-the-console-launcher).
After deployment, check both portal URLs and
rehearse scoring with a test team; a successful build alone is not that rehearsal.
Use the [event runbook](https://tenkacloud.com/docs/operate/run-an-event/index.en.html)
for team preparation and timing, and the
[launcher guide](https://github.com/susumutomita/TenkaCloud/blob/main/infrastructure/templates/README.md)
for settings and teardown. Console cleanup uses `ACTION=destroy-all`; follow the guide's data-retention instructions.
Deleting only the launcher leaves event resources running.
Local `make destroy` and `make destroy-all` also retain the source-bundle S3
bucket: its current bundle and retained versions keep incurring storage charges.
Identify the exact bucket from the deploy log, check that no other environment
uses it, and follow the deployment guide to empty all versions and delete markers
before removing an unused bucket. Shared CDK bootstrap resources are separate.
Do not promise zero cost or use teardown as a generic response to a deploy failure.

SaaS has a separate multi-tenant implementation. It is not the current first-event
self-service guide; consult the organizer manual's recorded verification limits.

## Read the code by the symptom

Paths below are relative to the platform checkout. Start with the affected row and
nearby tests, then trace callers and consumers. Do not scan the entire repository
before making a small change.

| Symptom or change | Entry point |
| --- | --- |
| Local startup or catalog availability | `scripts/tenkacloud-local.ts`, `scripts/local-play/` |
| Event/team setup | `apps/application-admin-console/src/pages/EventDetail.tsx` |
| Participant answer or score display | `apps/participant-portal/src/`, then `infrastructure/lib/problem-deploy/handlers/participant-handler/` |
| Deployment or backend configuration | `infrastructure/templates/lite-pipeline.yaml`, `scripts/tenkacloud-lite.ts`, `infrastructure/lib/problem-deploy/control-data/` |
| Problem rules, hints, or game UI | `problems/<category>/<problem>/metadata.json`, its runtime/plugin, and `portal/` |
| Shared API or scoring contract | `packages/portal-contracts/`, `packages/problem-sdk/`, corresponding producers and consumers |

For a checkout, read `AGENTS.md`; `CLAUDE.md` is just an import of it. Preserve the
parent and submodule revisions and unrelated work. Trace input → handler/rule →
stored state → displayed result. Report the actual failing step and evidence.
Required commit verification is `make before-commit`; use focused tests while editing.
Apply existing authorization and ask before unapproved destructive actions, releases,
shared-environment changes, or secret access. Read-only investigation can proceed.

## Prompts a user can give their assistant

- 「TenkaCloud をローカルで試したい。この端末の前提条件を確認して、問題を1つ開始し、回答の結果が見えるところまで進めて。」
- 「TenkaCloud を AWS に構築したい。DB 費用を抑える Turso の手順を使い、既存環境の有無と必要な設定を調べて。構成・費用・撤去方法を提示してからデプロイする。」
- 「この不具合について、画面から API、保存、得点表示までの関係を該当ファイルで説明して。根拠を確認してから修正し、実行した検証と未確認事項を分けて報告して。」

## Book

- [Build Your Own Cloud Competition (English)](https://leanpub.com/build-your-own-cloud-competition)
- [『自分で作るクラウド競技』(日本語)](https://zenn.dev/bull/books/cloud-competition)

These explain design decisions, **not** a specification. Current code and tests take precedence.
